authors: Francisco Javier Andrade Chavez; Gabriele Nava; Silvio Traversaro; Francesco Nori; Daniele Pucci
title: Model Based In Situ Calibration with Temperature compensation of 6 axis Force Torque Sensors
observation: Six-axis iCub calibration with temperature terms reduces mean residual external force magnitude from the workbench value 10.46 N to 3.987 N in a no-external-contact leg segment.
limitation: The reference is the zero external force expected from dynamics between hip and ankle. It is not a wrist load-cell ground truth during assembly contact. Compare the expanded Sensors paper as same study family.
rights: Public arXiv author manuscript. Link and summary.

authors: Francisco Javier Andrade Chavez; Silvio Traversaro; Daniele Pucci
title: Six-Axis Force Torque Sensor Model-Based In Situ Calibration Method and Its Impact in Floating-Based Robot Dynamic Performance
locator: Offset validation and Fig. 10; discussion of single-foot balancing
observation: The extended iCub study evaluates temperature-aware offsets about a month after calibration and across balancing trials at 26.6, 36.2 and 43.5 °C. Improvements in the estimated external wrench depend on axis and calibration choice.
limitation: Related paper shares method and robot with the ICRA report. These temperature conditions cannot be counted as independent wrist-assembly datasets.
